newAdvisories.title: A timed-out reference child leaves the previous run per-script report on disk under the same name
newAdvisories.firstFailingBoundary: the child spawn loop: the target report path is never cleared before subprocess.run
newAdvisories.counterexample: check-identity.py exceeds the 600s budget on a slow host. The launcher correctly records timedOut true, exitCode null, reportSha256 null and passed false. But foundation/identity-report.json from an earlier successful run remains on disk carrying its own {"passed": 1596, "failed": 0}. Nothing distinguishes it from a current result by inspection of that file alone.
newAdvisories.owningSelector: run-reference-checks.py, the loop over the five (script, report) pairs
newAdvisories.assessment: This is bounded and already partly discharged. The launcher own report declines attribution and its docstring states this exact hazard verbatim. I searched every .py in the corpus outside reviews/ and the ONLY consumer of those five report filenames is the launcher itself, so no in-corpus reader can be misled. The exposure is to an external or human reader, or to a future application step that reads a per-script report directly.
newAdvisories.remedy: Unlink the target report (missing_ok) immediately before each spawn, or write each run into a fresh per-run report directory. That would make "no completed result is attributed" and "no stale bytes are present" coincide instead of relying on the reader consulting the launcher report.
newAdvisories.notARegression: Advisory rather than SHOULD: the launcher report is honest, the limitation is published on the file, and no consumer inside the reviewed corpus reads the stale artifact.

CB-GAP-1.basis: At-most-one-per-registered-row is enforced at three places on these bytes. Two share one helper: foundation/identity-model.py:93 admit_parameter_selection, called by native_evidence_model.v2.py:4031 (pre-Plan admit_analysis_spec step 4) and identity-model.py:1679 (open_run_closure over the retained analysis-spec). The third is the independent workflows_model.v1.py verify_scope_parameter_binding. I called that real entrypoint: zero rows legal at the helper, one row verifies, two distinct rows over the registered ScopeDocumentV1 digest refuse CONFIG.INVALID. Distinct registered rows coexist (scope+import = 2). Whole-item duplicates refuse earlier on uniqueItems + canonical-set. Unregistered rows are left to PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_UNREGISTERED (identity-model.py:811) and two rows per digest to PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW (:809). ImportSourceContext keeps its own guard inside the consuming derivation; stage parameters are a Plan subset.
CB-GAP-1.scope: Enforcement presence, control flow and real-entrypoint behaviour. Not product-host reachability.

CB-GAP-2.basis: x-opensip-uniqueness on #/$defs/analysis-spec/properties/requestedCapabilities carries ownershipTuple [capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot] with requiredness stated as an attribute and no last-wins/merge. Internal key native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple is present in native_evidence_model.v2.py and registered in native-evidence.schemas.v2.json x-opensip-public-route-registry, adding no DomainDetailCode member. CB-GAP-3.basis: I independently counted the ladder authority: 13 relations, 17 registered (relation,rung) pairs, 5 resolved and 12 non-resolved - the exact partition the contract states. RC-6 is coded as an implication (native_evidence_model.v2.py: if entry["coverage"]=="complete" and rc.get("examinedExhaustive") is not True), leaving coverage=unknown unconstrained in both directions. It is decided in coverage_bijection, which admit_coverage_result_v3 calls at the producer boundary and which identity-model.py re-runs over the retained payload at Run closure. Controls sweep all 17 pairs fact-free, and separate named controls exercise the producer boundary and retained closure on the reproduced file@enumerated vector in both minting universes with the fault list asserted to be RC-6 alone. RC-0 still outranks it; RC-2/RC-3 positives preserved.
CB-GAP-3.scope: Enumeration completeness stays distinct from resolution completeness. The 17-pair sweep is helper-level by construction; sealed-Run coverage is the narrower named vectors, exactly as the controls label themselves.

CB-GAP-4.basis: Both outputDomains arrays $ref #/$defs/Domain, a flat 32-member enum equal to Ref.properties.domain and to the byDomain key set; agreement is enforced at closure by equal_typed -> STAGE_SPEC_OUTPUT_DOMAIN_JOIN (identity-model.py:1487), so equality is separate from membership. The stage-spec record commits planId, producerClosure, operation, parameters, outputDomains and outputSchemaDigest, so no uncommitted discriminator remains.

NEW-SHOULD-1.basis: I moved exactly one law - the at-most-one ambiguity guard - below the payload-digest match in a disposable copy and re-called the REAL owning entrypoint. Of seven scenarios exactly ONE changed: two rows plus a NON-candidate document regressed from CONFIG.INVALID to BASELINE.SCOPE_PARAMETER_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Both candidate-holder scenarios were unchanged, which is the direct demonstration that the old controls could not hold the order. Running check-identity.py against the mutated tree gave exit 1 and 1594 passed / 2 failed, the two failures being precisely an-ambiguous-spec-refuses-as-ambiguous-even-for-a-document-that-is-neither-candidate and the-three-answers-for-one-non-candidate-document-stay-distinct-by-row-multiplicity. The removed source-text-count control was a cross-file string tally establishing nothing semantic; its removal is correct and the behavioural carrier/registry controls are retained.
NEW-SHOULD-1.scope: Mutation of the real admission, not a copied algorithm and not a manufactured error. Mutated bytes and diff retained.
